note: Which host a Reality node fronts, as measured rather than chosen. This is the one place the measurement lives: provision-reality-node.rb takes its default and its refusal from here, check-node-in-fleet.py reports a published node fronting a host measured unusable, and the add-tono-node skill points at this file. Re-measuring updates all three at once.
measurement: A probe inside the mainland completed a verified TLS 1.3 handshake to every host under `usable`, and to none of the hosts under `unusable`. Nothing else in the flow can catch a bad choice: the provisioner's precheck runs on the VPS, the post-install data-plane test runs on the operator's machine, and the fleet audit only compares the catalog against the box — so both are wrong together and agree.
matching: `usable` holds the exact hosts that were measured. `unusable` holds registrable domains and covers every subdomain of them, because it is the whole property that failed, not one name under it.
latency: Node-to-front latency is nearly irrelevant and easy to optimise by mistake: the client never contacts the front, only the node does, and only when answering an active probe.
